original_target.title: Are polynomial Fischer operators bijective on all entire functions?
original_target.area: Complex analysis and potential theory; holomorphic partial differential equations

full_original_statement:
Let $`d\ge2`$ and let $`E(\mathbb C^d)`$ denote all entire holomorphic functions, without a growth restriction. For a nonzero polynomial $`P(z)=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha z^\alpha`$, define

```math
P^*(z)=\sum_\alpha\overline{a_\alpha}z^\alpha,
\qquad P^*(D)=\sum_\alpha\overline{a_\alpha}\partial_z^\alpha.
```

Must the operator

```math
F_P:E(\mathbb C^d)\longrightarrow E(\mathbb C^d),
\qquad F_P(q)=P^*(D)(Pq)
```

be a bijection for every such $`P`$? Thus every entire forcing $`g`$ should have exactly one entire solution $`q`$ to $`P^*(D)(Pq)=g`$.

The operator uses the whole coefficient-conjugated polynomial, not only its leading homogeneous part. The zero polynomial is excluded. Nonzero constants are immediate affirmative cases.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual primary conjecture uses the WHOLE P* differential operator on every entire function. Current low-order Fischer decompositions use growth restrictions and/or only the principal homogeneous part. Polynomial-data/Fock-space results do not establish existence and uniqueness for all entire forcing. No complete matching new theorem identified.
